item.content:
Syllabus For Fundamental Of C-Programming

  • Token in C-programming
  • Keywords/Operators/String/Constant/Identifier
  • Special Character
  • int, char, float (signed and unsigned), short and long

Tokens in C

  1. Keywords
  2. Operators
  3. Identifiers
  4. Constants
  5. Special Symbols
  6. String

Keywords

  • auto, double, int, struct, switch ……. (total 32)

Identifier

  • Name of a variable || Name of a function.
constraint for identifier
  1. Can’t be start with digit, only letter || underscore followed by digit
  2. No special keyword should be used.

C is a Case sensitive language a and A are treaated different.

Constants/Literals

int a = 08; In above example ‘08’ is a Constant.

Q Solve

#include <stdio.h>

int main() {
	int a ;
	a = 60+0b1111+014+0x10;
	printf("%d", a);                         // 103
	
	return 0;
}

Explanation 60 <– Decimal Constant; 0b <– Binary Constant 0 <– Octal Constant 0x <– Hexadecimal Constant

🔢 Number System Recap

If you don’t know Number Systems, here’s a quick recap.

Decimal Number

In C, an integer constant without a prefix is treated as a decimal constant.

printf("%d", 40);
Binary Number Calculation
Binary Number -> 0b1111

  1    1    1    1
  ↓    ↓    ↓    ↓
 2³   2²   2¹   2⁰

= 1×8 + 1×4 + 1×2 + 1×1
= 8 + 4 + 2 + 1
= 15
Octal Number Calculation
Octal Number-> 014

014₈
= 1 × 8¹ + 4 × 8⁰
= 1 × 8 + 4 × 1
= 8 + 4
= 12₁₀
Hexadecimal Number Calculation
Hexadecimal -> 0x

0x10₁₆
= 1 × 16¹ + 0 × 16⁰
= 1 × 16 + 0 × 1
= 16

Q Solve

#include <stdio.h>

int main() {
	int a ;
	a = 0101/011+0110+0x110;
	printf("%d", a);                          // 351
	
	return 0;
}
Format Specifier
Format Specifier Data Type Example
%d Signed integer printf("%d", 10);
%i Signed integer printf("%i", 10);
%u Unsigned integer printf("%u", 20);
%f Float printf("%f", 3.14);
%lf Double (scanf) scanf("%lf", &d);
%c Character printf("%c", 'A');
%s String printf("%s", "Hello");
%x Hexadecimal (lowercase) printf("%x", 255); → ff
%X Hexadecimal (uppercase) printf("%X", 255); → FF
%o Octal printf("%o", 8); → 10
%p Pointer address printf("%p", ptr);
%% Prints % symbol printf("100%%");
DATA TYPE
  1. The value it takes
  2. Amount of memory required
  3. Interpretation of value
Signed and Unsigned Number

example: 2s compliment Integer Interpretation 1111 (Signed) -1x2^3 + 1x2^2 + 1x2^1

11111 (UnSigned) 1x2^3 + 1x2^2 + 1x2^1

2’s Complement — Signed Integer
  • MSB (Most Significant Bit) = 0 → Positive
  • MSB = 1 → Negative
  • MSB weight = -2ⁿ⁻¹
  • Other bits have normal positive weights.

Example: 4-bit 1111

Weights: -8  4  2  1
Bits:     1  1  1  1

= -8 + 4 + 2 + 1
= -1

Range of a Integer –> -2^n-1 to 2^n-1

Operators & Arithmetic Expression

`+, -, *, /, % "

/ -> Quotient % -> Remainder

Dividend = Quotient Divisor + Remainder*

Solve–> 7/3, -7/3, 7/-3. -7/-3

If dividend and divisor same sign +ve otherwise -ve Remainder: Sign of dividend is sign of Remainder

Solve

#include<stdio.h>

int main(){
	int x;
	x= -2 + 11 - 7 * 9 % 6 / 12;       //9
	printf("%d",x);
	return 0;
}
C Operator Precedence — Short
Priority Operators Associativity
1 () Left → Right
2 ++ -- ! ~ Right → Left
3 * / % Left → Right
4 + - Left → Right
5 < <= > >= Left → Right
6 == != Left → Right
7 && Left → Right
8 ` ` Left → Right
9 = += -= *= /= Right → Left

Higher priority = evaluated first.

* / % have same precedence → evaluate left to right.

Functions In C

`A function is a block of code which only runs when it is called.

*Input (function parameters) and output (return value) of function.

  1. Function Declaration
    1. Announcement that this function we are going to use.
    2. It has function name, input parameters, number of parameters, types of output.
  2. Function Definition
    1. Has code of function.
  3. Function Call
    1. Function calling (execute)

Declaration Of Function

return_type name(parameter_type1, parameter_type2......);

example:-

float func_name(int a_argument, int b_argument, float c_argument){

};

int * func1 (int *){};

int func (void){};  // no parameters

int func(){};

void func(){};  // if output is not present then use void before func declaration

Function Definition

Actually piece of code.

#include<stdio.h>

float areaOfCircle(float radius){
	float  area  = 3.14*(radius*radius);
	return area;
}

void main(){
	float r;
	printf("Enter the radius: ");
	scanf("%f",&r);
	printf("Area of Circle: %f",areaOfCircle(r));
	
}

Type of Parameter Passing

  1. Call by Value
  2. Call by reference
  3. Call by address

Call by Value
